title: Planning with the environment
message: A shared representation connects material, candidate actions and execution.
speaker_notes: Show the pinned 55-object scene. Frame the complete thesis: 2D foundation, action selection, rover execution and shared operation. The live demonstration is one component of the talk.

title: Why material rearrangement matters
message: A useful push may deliver material or prepare a later collection.
speaker_notes: Use the broom-and-dustpan intuition. State the question before introducing the field. Keep the mission objective open; do not imply that high heat guarantees reduced time.

title: Relation to aggregate-forming planning
message: Build on the lab context while distinguishing the present representation.
speaker_notes: Briefly position Shaked et al. (2023). The current lab-inspired comparison is partial. Save detailed comparator fidelity for questions.

title: Cells and visible successors
message: A target-facing successor graph defines possible collection steps.
speaker_notes: Use the same source (0,15) as the live demo. Explain counts, cell centers, target angle 45 degrees, range gate 1 and monotone progress. The cone is not the whole eligibility rule. State that these are the pinned dense-scene settings, not the small corridor settings.

title: Candidate routes and shared continuations
message: Search collects material; nearer solved continuations can be reused.
speaker_notes: Trace (0,15) → (6,10) → (8,10) → (9,10), gathering four new objects. Explain raw count ranking, distance tie-breaking and the configured factor-2 target-length cap. Briefly show suffix reuse without claiming global optimality.

title: Directional value becomes heat
message: The field combines propagated route value and directional alignment.
speaker_notes: Introduce maximum propagation, normalized headings and one heat equation. Here own heat weight is 0 and alignment exponent is 1. Distinguish heat from local material and from predicted time savings. Pygame colors auto-rescale: use numerical values for before/after comparisons.

title: How staging uses the field
message: Heat and proximity identify possible intermediate destinations.
speaker_notes: Explain the 0.7 heat / 0.3 proximity anchor score and source/anchor heat thresholds. The live action will be a target push, chosen to make selective updating easy to follow. Staging policy evidence is discussed later; do not add a second live action here.

title: LIVE DEMO — reveal, execute, update
message: A changed scene can retain unaffected target paths while updating dependent sources.
speaker_notes: Talk minutes 11–17. Follow live_demo/DEMO_RUNBOOK.html: visibility 0:00–1:30; route 1:30–2:20; vectors/heat 2:20–3:10; execute once and inspect E/D/R 3:10–4:40; explain reuse 4:40–5:20; return to slides by 6:00. Source is (0,15), four new deliveries, 8 target searches versus 47 fresh. Full verification passes. Start seminar demo.cmd restores the pinned scene and display preset. Hard stop at minute 17; if behind, skip vectors. If a technical problem occurs, use the six saved screenshots instead of debugging. Keep spillage off and parameters fixed in the main demo.

title: The transport estimator is replaceable
message: Route geometry and material state feed a model that predicts deposits and yield.
speaker_notes: Describe the current curvature/load estimator, coefficient and threshold. Explain the replacement contract and sampling/capacity limitations. Spillage toggling is optional after-talk interaction, not part of the six-minute demo. Do not invent an observed retention result.

title: What the computational evidence establishes
message: Fewer target searches and measured runtime are different claims.
speaker_notes: Separate the live verified search-count reduction from the historical timing chart. Mark the latter historical. Mention the 96 sequence checks without presenting them as a general proof. Heat, propagation and staging rebuild globally; the editor also runs full verification. A clean timing study remains a separate evaluation.

title: From a useful path to an executed task
message: The 2D representation is the foundation for the later work.
speaker_notes: At minute 21 switch decisively to the rover pipeline. End the foundation block by minute 22. Next: approach/alignment/tracking, collision recovery, policies, lookahead, team operation and estimation.

title: Make a planned push executable
message: Approach, alignment, shovel operation and path following connect the field to the rover.
speaker_notes: Use a verified rover clip with planned and measured trajectories overlaid. Explain the phases of a push and why a useful 2D path is not automatically an executable motion. Show low-level tracking, alignment and completion/recovery decisions. Use advisor_demo_20261019/advisor_guide.html and the execution-signal inventory as evidence sources. Clip selection remains pending; this is substantive completed engineering, not merely future work.

title: Avoid collisions and recover progress
message: Execution must handle other rovers, blocked approaches and unfinished actions.
speaker_notes: Show a state sequence: approach conflict → yield or recovery → resume or reassign. Separate collision avoidance from task allocation, and delivery from final parking. Use research/multi_rover/AFTER_REPAIR_VALIDATION_20261017.md for a bounded validation example. Zero detected contacts in a tested cohort does not establish a universal safety guarantee. Select one logged recovery example; do not stage an unverified success.

title: Choose between delivery and staging
message: The same environment representation supports different action-selection policies.
speaker_notes: Return briefly to the side pile to explain the decision, then show evidence from the repaired highway and policy-mode studies. Sources: lab_experiments/HIGHWAY_REPAIRED_EXPERIMENT_RECORD_2026-10-03.md and POLICY_MODE_CONFIRMATION_FINDINGS_2026-10-04.md. Show the tradeoff between endpoint completion and limited time/travel budgets. These studies are already completed; selecting the final seminar graph is pending, not the existence of results. Preserve matched-cohort denominators and do not treat every added policy term as an improvement.

title: Look ahead to the next useful push
message: Predict a changed environment, replan, and evaluate a short action sequence.
speaker_notes: Extend the running example into a two-action tree: direct delivery versus stage then collect. Label this schematic until actual candidate scores are exported. Execute only the first real action and observe again. Discuss the 32-run pilot in research/lookahead/EXPERIMENT_REFERENCE_20261006.md: eight paired scenarios and one seed; deeper search has computation and spill costs and frequent fallbacks. It is preliminary evidence, not a general winner. Separate planning depth from accuracy of the successor model.

title: Share the environment between rovers
message: A common field supplies tasks; allocation and execution determine team behavior.
speaker_notes: Show one shared map, candidate tasks, assignment and reassignment. Use research/multi_rover/LARGE_RANDOM_CAMPAIGN_20261017.md: the 200-run allocation study compares normal and selective handoff on 100 matched pairs. It is not a controlled fleet-size speedup study. Discuss completion, contention, parking and operating limits. Retain the unresolved four-rover case as a limitation. Select a logged team clip and a matched allocation plot; do not claim a robust overall policy winner.

title: Estimate execution cost without fixing the objective
message: Timing estimates provide inputs for later decision criteria.
speaker_notes: Explain approach, alignment, pushing and overhead. Distinguish predicted from measured time and identify where calibration is weak. Keep the optimization criterion open. T_q, if shown, belongs to evaluation and means time to deliver fraction q. Timing is one foundation alongside retention and task feasibility, not the declared thesis objective.

title: Bring the evidence together
message: Evaluate the foundation, action selection and rover execution at their own levels.
speaker_notes: Use three columns: 2D computation; policy/rollout outcomes; rover/team execution. Reuse the completed highway, policy and allocation studies with their recorded limitations. Mark only genuine gaps as pending: matched selective/full timing, broader equivalence tests, retention calibration, final choice of illustrative clips and any remaining reference-control experiments. Final thesis emphasis and conclusions remain open for advisor discussion.

title: One framework, several levels of decisions
message: The heatmap is the foundation of the planning-and-execution story.
speaker_notes: Close with the chain: environment representation → candidate generation → action selection/lookahead → rover control → shared operation → updated observation. Summarize demonstrated benefits and operating limits from the selected evidence; do not invent a final experimental conclusion.
